Staff.title: Staff
Staff.description: Represents a staff member with their details and schedule information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Staff entity.

name.description: The name of the staff member.

calendarId.description: Reference to a calendar ID associated with the staff member.

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer with their contact and location information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Customer entity.

latitude.description: The latitude of the customer's address.

longitude.description: The longitude of the customer's address.

Schedule.title: Schedule
Schedule.description: Represents a work schedule, linking staff, customers, and location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Schedule entity.

startTime.description: The start time of the schedule.

endTime.description: The end time of the schedule.

StatusUpdate.title: StatusUpdate
StatusUpdate.description: Represents a real-time status update for an employee.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StatusUpdate entity.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the status update.

action.description: The action performed by the employee (e.g., Arrive, begin task, finish task, depart).

latitude.description: The latitude of the employee's location.

longitude.description: The longitude of the employee's location.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to optimize security, scalability, and debuggability, adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC, and QAPs. Authorization independence is achieved through denormalization of authorization data. Homogeneous security postures are created by segregating data based on access requirements, and access models are standardized using path-based ownership and membership maps.

**Authorization Independence:**
The design avoids using `get()` calls in security rules by denormalizing authorization data. For example, if access to `Schedules` needs to be controlled based on the `Staff` or `Customer`, the relevant attributes are duplicated/copied into the `Schedule` documents, eliminating the need to retrieve parent documents in rules.

**Segregation and QAPs:**
Data is segregated into collections based on its security posture. Path-based ownership (`/staff/{staffId}/statusUpdates/{statusUpdateId}`) is used for private data. This approach makes `list` operations secure because the security rules can easily restrict access to only the resources owned by the requesting user, fulfilling the QAPs requirement.

**Membership Maps (Not explicitly used but considered):**
If there were collaborative entities, membership maps (`members: {uid1: "role", uid2: "role"}`) would be employed. However, based on the defined entities, simple ownership models are sufficient.

**Global Roles (DBAC):**
Global roles are implemented using dedicated collections like `/roles_admin/{uid}`. The existence of a document in this collection grants admin privileges.

**Invariants:**
The structure supports data integrity by enforcing ownership (using paths), leveraging server timestamps, and denormalizing key attributes to maintain consistency across documents.
